places.name: Studio Ghibli
places.connection: The animation studio where the film was produced. This was the first official film released under the Studio Ghibli name.

places.name: Welsh Valleys (e.g., Rhondda Valley)
places.connection: Miyazaki visited Welsh mining towns during the 1984 miners' strikes and was deeply moved. The experience directly inspired the design and communal spirit of Pazu's mining town.

places.name: Paronella Park
places.connection: The lush, moss-covered ruins of a castle in this park are cited as a visual inspiration for the overgrown, garden-like upper levels of Laputa.

places.name: Caernarfon Castle
places.connection: The imposing medieval architecture of this castle is believed to have influenced the design of the military fortress where Sheeta is held captive.

places.name: Machu Picchu
places.connection: The iconic Incan citadel's integration with its mountain environment is a likely aesthetic inspiration for the ruins of Laputa.

places.name: Angkor Wat
places.connection: The image of giant tree roots reclaiming ancient stone temples at Angkor Wat is strongly echoed in the design of Laputa's central, giant tree.

places.name: Sigiriya
places.connection: This ancient rock fortress, built atop a massive column of rock, provides a real-world parallel to a city built in a high, inaccessible location, likely serving as conceptual inspiration.

places.name: Metéora
places.connection: The dramatic landscape of monasteries built atop natural rock pillars mirrors the verticality and sense of isolated civilization seen in the film.

places.name: Big Pit National Coal Museum
places.connection: A real former coal mine that exemplifies the kind of industrial heritage and environment that inspired Pazu's hometown and occupation.

places.name: The Old Man of Storr
places.connection: The dramatic, otherworldly rock formations and misty landscapes of Skye are often cited by fans and critics as a possible visual influence on the film's fantastical scenery.
